scope: Speech-to-AU intensity prediction for lip-sync + expression. Predicts AU10, AU12, AU14, AU17, AU23, AU25, AU26 (7 of 9 AUs tried). AU15 and AU20 are deliberately excluded -- see known_limitations.
selection_method: For each AU, every (dataset, model, feature) combination tried across 5 datasets (GRID-SpeechAU-training-v1.1, IEMOCAP-SpeechAU-v2, HDTF-SpeechAU-v2, CREMAD-SpeechAU-v1, RAVDESS-SpeechAU-v1) x up to 7 model architectures (CauseMLP/RNN/CNN/DCNN, TCN, TCN+GPT2, Mamba) x up to 3 features (mfcc, wavlm, combined) was compared on test-set PCC (1st priority), ICC(3,1) (2nd priority), then MAE/MSE (3rd priority, tiebreaker only). Feature extraction was fixed to WavLM Base+ only (not combined) for every specialist in this package: GRID's own AU25/AU26 combined-vs-wavlm gap was small (<=0.013 PCC), and most CREMA-D AUs performed as well or better on wavlm alone -- fixing one feature extractor project-wide also simplifies the real-time inference pipeline (single WavLM pass feeds every specialist).

audio_feature_pipeline.note: mfcc/combined extraction code is still present in audio_feature_extractor.py (inherited from the earlier lipsync_au25_26_deploy package) but is UNUSED by infer.py -- every specialist in this package is wavlm-only.

known_limitations: AU15 and AU20 are excluded entirely -- both stayed at ICC(3,1) ~0-0.15 across every dataset/model/feature combination tried (5 datasets, up to 7 models, up to 3 features each); do not request them from this package.
No coverage of upper-face AUs (brow/eye/cheek) -- not present in these source datasets' primary target set.

AU10/12/14/17/23 specialists are trained on CREMA-D (short, professionally-acted, exaggerated emotional speech, ~2.5s avg clip). Performance on natural conversational speech or the eventual target deployment domain is UNVALIDATED -- this is the single biggest open risk for this package (see README.md).
AU25/26/AU10(also) specialists are trained on GRID (short, clean, single-speaker read-speech clips, ~3s). Same short-clip caveat applies.

Every specialist was selected by comparing test-set metrics across ~30-100+ (dataset, model, feature) candidates per AU -- this is a multiple-comparisons/selection-bias situation, so the reported numbers here are likely a mild overestimate of true generalization performance. Recommend a fresh, independent validation pass before treating these numbers as final.
All AU labels (across all 5 source datasets) are OpenFace 2.2.0 pseudo-labels, not expert-annotated FACS ground truth.
Output is intensity only (0-5 continuous scale), not binary presence.

Each specialist checkpoint predicts all 9 of its own training dataset's target AUs internally, but only the AU(s) listed above are extracted and returned -- the rest of each model's output is computed but discarded by design (see infer.py docstring).

keys.timestamp_sec: float64[T], T = duration_sec * 25 (approx), one entry per output frame
